title: WIP: Add NV GPTQ W4AFP8 lifecycle and encoded activation streams
body:
## Summary

WIP implementation of GPTQ W4AFP8 for NVIDIA GB10 (SM121), with per-token E4M3 activation scaling and native INT32-packed GPTQ INT4 checkpoint weights.

- Stage centered INT4 weight codes losslessly into a nonpersistent E4M3 cache during post-init; reuse it during inference.
- Use native FP8 GEMM operands with FP32 accumulation, applying each original GPTQ group scale before summing groups.
- Add versioned activation configuration, backend selection, calibration replay, packing, save/load, and post-init lifecycle support.
- Carry encoded activations and token scales between selected Llama decoder layers, share inputs across Q/K/V and gate/up, and reject plain tensors at selected Linear inputs.
- Add GB10 fused kernels, full-model coverage audits, paired full-row quality tooling, and a memory guard with a 2 GiB reserve and swap disabled.

This PR contains only W4AFP8. W4A4/NVFP4 experiments are excluded.

## Activation contract and current scope

Version 3 carries FP8 codes plus FP32 token scales across decoder layers and into all selected GEMMs. RMSNorm and residual arithmetic decode internally to FP32 and encode their outputs. Linear outputs feeding attention, nonlinear functions, or residual arithmetic use model dtype. RoPE, attention, KV cache, and the output head retain wider precision. This is not a claim of FP8 arithmetic throughout every decoder operation.

Initial support: Llama, Linux, GB10/SM121, symmetric INT4 with group size 128, contiguous groups, `desc_act=False`, INT32 packing, and an unquantized output head. Runtime memory includes the derived FP8 weight cache. No end-to-end speedup claim is made.

## Validation

Tested the extracted FP8 branch after rebasing onto upstream `6d3232c`:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| FP8 kernel/config tests | 14 passed |
| Encoded activation stream tests | 6 passed |
| Calibration replay tests | 12 passed |
| Tiny Llama quantize/save/reload, with and without rotation | 2 passed |
| Saved Llama 3.2 1B reload | 1 passed |
| Stage and rotation tests | 40 passed, 1 optional checkpoint test skipped |
| Full-model activation audit | All 16 layers and 112 projections passed, including shared carrier pointers and cached generation |

Total: **75 passed, 1 skipped**. Compile checks, shell syntax checks, and `git diff --check` passed. Guarded runs stayed above the 2 GiB reserve with zero swap.

Independent Torch oracles cover FP16/BF16 GEMM inputs, group-specific and per-column scales, zero inputs, outliers, and partial tiles. GEMM cases include K=256, N=64/96/128 and M=1/3/7/16/33; encoding cases include widths 128/256 and up to 129 rows. FP8 threshold and neighboring-value checks cover FP16, BF16, and FP32, including signed zero. Complete encoded bytes match exactly in those tests; floating checks use quantization tolerances of 1e-6 and inference tolerances of at most 2e-3. Per-test maximum floating errors were not separately recorded. The optional microbenchmark uses CUDA graph replay; it is not an end-to-end performance result.

### Existing full-row GSM8K Platinum evidence

The fresh version-3 checkpoint used 512 calibration records, 188,256 nonpadding tokens, and concatenation size 2,048. Both evaluation lanes use the same packed weights.

| Metric | Result |
| --- | --- |
| W4A16 baseline | 432 / 1,209 = 35.7320% |
| W4AFP8 | 441 / 1,209 = 36.4764% |
| Paired difference | +0.7444 percentage points |
| Paired 95% confidence interval | [-1.5431, +3.0319] percentage points |
| Baseline-only / FP8-only correct | 95 / 104 |
| Provisional 2-point regression budget | Within budget |

These full-row results predate the FP8-only extraction and were **not rerun for this PR**. The focused tests and full-model activation audit above were rerun on the extracted branch. The score difference does not establish a statistically significant improvement. GSM8K Platinum is the acceptance benchmark; ARC is diagnostic.

## WIP follow-up

- Review lifecycle integration and the explicit mixed-precision operator boundaries.
- Repeat full-row quality evaluation if review changes numerical behavior.
- Measure end-to-end prefill/decode performance and runtime memory before making performance claims.
- Expand architecture and hardware support separately.

See `docs/gptq-w4a-gb10.md` for usage, boundary details, and reproducible validation commands.

title: Add packed FP8 inference kernels for MLX
body:
## Summary

- add `MlxFP8PackedLinear`, a packed Metal inference runtime that consumes the checkpoint's original FP8 bytes without expanding them to dense FP16 weights
- support every GPTQModel FP8 storage format: E4M3FN, E5M2, E4M3FNUZ, E5M2FNUZ, and E8M0FNU
- support tensor, row, and block inverse-scale layouts
- keep MLX's official MXFP8 `nn.QuantizedLinear` path for compatible E4M3FN tensor/row checkpoints
- use a vectorized packed GEMV kernel for decode and a simdgroup-matrix path for eligible prefill shapes
- preserve FP16/BF16 activation and output dtypes; scales and accumulation remain FP32
- retain `FP8MlxQuantLinear` as the BaseQuantLinear holder/validator and auto-select this runtime through the existing MLX backend
- reduce fallback weight storage from 2 bytes/weight to 1 byte/weight (50%)

This is intentionally one quantization-method PR: FP8 only.

## Correctness fix

Current main dequantizes unsupported FP8 layouts to FP16 before MLX inference. For realistic E5M2 row inverse scales above FP16 max (65,504), that cast becomes infinity and the dense weight becomes zero. The packed path retains scales in FP32 and avoids that failure.

The benchmark below uses E5M2 row scales in the 600,000–609,999 range to exercise that real failure mode. Main therefore has relative L2 error 1.0; packed inference remains close to a float64 decode/matmul oracle.

| Output dtype | Packed max abs error | Packed max relative L2 | Main max relative L2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| FP16 | 1.53e-5 | 2.10e-4 | 1.0 |
| BF16 | 1.22e-4 | 1.71e-3 | 1.0 |

## Performance vs current main

Hardware: Apple M5 Ultra. Software: MLX 0.32.2, Torch 2.14.0. Base: `388f8acd7`. Each number is the median of 31 paired, alternating measurements after 7 warmups. Speedup is `main dense ms / packed ms`; values above 1 are faster.

| Qwen3.8-27B projection | FP16 r1 | FP16 r16 | BF16 r1 | BF16 r16 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| full_attn.q_proj | 1.041x | 1.087x | 2.841x | 1.690x |
| full_attn.k_proj | 1.028x | 1.229x | 1.200x | 1.339x |
| full_attn.v_proj | 1.032x | 1.253x | 1.168x | 1.346x |
| full_attn.o_proj | 0.932x | 0.812x | 1.922x | 1.284x |
| linear_attn.in_proj_qkv | 1.081x | 0.997x | 2.563x | 1.475x |
| linear_attn.out_proj | 0.971x | 0.816x | 1.907x | 1.248x |
| mlp.gate_proj | 1.135x | 0.754x | 3.576x | 1.424x |
| mlp.up_proj | 1.230x | 0.723x | 3.495x | 1.459x |
| mlp.down_proj | 1.173x | 0.474x | 3.343x | 1.185x |
| **Geomean** | **1.065x** | **0.870x** | **2.264x** | **1.376x** |

| Aggregate sum of per-shape medians | Main | Packed |
|---|---:|---:|
| FP16, rows=1 | 3.0459 ms | 2.8330 ms |
| FP16, rows=16 | 3.9334 ms | 4.8426 ms |
| BF16, rows=1 | 6.1070 ms | 2.4286 ms |
| BF16, rows=16 | 6.8011 ms | 4.9194 ms |

FP16 prefill is an explicit tradeoff on the widest projections; the packed runtime provides correct E5M2 inference and halves weight memory where main's dense fallback is invalid. BF16 is faster on every tested projection and batch shape.

Weight memory is exactly halved for every projection (for example, each MLP projection is 170 MiB on main versus 85 MiB packed).

## Coverage

- all 5 FP8 formats × tensor/row/block scaling × FP16/BF16 outputs
- exhaustive decode of all 256 byte values for every format
- all 9 Qwen3.8-27B projection shapes at rows=1 and rows=16 in FP16 and BF16
- existing official MLX MXFP8 path regression coverage
- loader integration and packed-byte retention checks
- SPDX and upstream FP8/Qwen credit headers on every changed/new file

## Validation

- `97 passed, 81 deselected` focused FP8 suite after the final loader cleanup
- `3517 passed` complete `tests/test_mlx_*.py` suite
- Ruff passed on all 6 changed files
- `git diff --check` passed

Benchmark command:

```bash
python tests/benchmark_mlx_qwen38_fp8_packed.py --dtype float16
python tests/benchmark_mlx_qwen38_fp8_packed.py --dtype bfloat16
```

title: Speed up BitsAndBytes 4-bit processor packing with MLX
body:
## Summary

Route large BitsAndBytes NF4/FP4 weights through the existing native MLX quantizer from the standard `BitsAndBytesLinear.pack_original` processor on Apple silicon.

The dominant weight quantization runs on MLX. Compressed nested statistics stay on the much smaller CPU scale vector, which preserves the exact bitsandbytes reduction and serialized state. Weights below 4,194,304 elements remain on the existing Torch/bitsandbytes path because MLX does not win below that measured crossover.

## What Changed

- Added an Apple-silicon MLX bridge for standard BitsAndBytes NF4/FP4 processor packing.
- Preserved exact bitsandbytes `QuantState` layouts for compressed and uncompressed statistics.
- Added a measured crossover guard so small weights retain the faster existing path.
- Added processor boundary/oracle tests for NF4/FP4, FP16/BF16, and both statistics modes.
- Added a reproducible Qwen3.8-27B benchmark covering every projection shape.
- INT8 is intentionally unchanged: end-to-end screening did not beat Torch on the smallest Qwen projections.

## Tests

Every working PR must include at least one new simple, fast, targeted unit test when the change affects behavior, a bug fix, or a regression path.

- [x] Unit tests have been executed and passed, or the reason they are not applicable is documented.
- [x] I added a new simple/fast unit test for this change, or documented why that is not applicable.


## Review Requirements

- [x] Avoided unnecessary monkeypatching and used the project's normal extension points where possible.
- [x] Minimized and compacted the impacted code surface.

title: Add native packed EXL3 inference kernels for MLX
body:
## Summary

- replaces EXL3's decoded FP16 MLX fallback with native packed-trellis inference
- adds a dedicated single-token Metal kernel and a 16-row SIMD-group matrix kernel
- transfers trellis/sign/bias tensors directly, including legacy `su`/`sv` sign bitfields
- supports every EXL3 bit width (1–8) and all three codebooks (`3inst`, `mcg`, `mul1`)
- preserves FP16/BF16 activation output dtype

The kernels extract each 16-bit cyclic trellis state directly from its packed bit window, decode the EXL3 codebook in Metal, and apply the existing native normalized Hadamard transforms. No dense weight is materialized.

## Qwen3.8-27B performance vs main

Apple M5 Ultra, MLX 0.32.2, 4-bit MCG, 31 paired alternating samples per case. Main is commit `6a4379e40` and uses the existing decoded FP16 `nn.Linear` fallback. Speedup is main latency / PR latency, so values above 1 are faster.

| Activation | Rows | Main median | Packed median | Median paired speedup | Geomean speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| FP16 | 1 | 0.2640 ms | 0.5215 ms | 0.473x | 0.478x |
| FP16 | 16 | 0.4681 ms | 0.6825 ms | 0.565x | 0.579x |
| BF16 | 1 | 0.7072 ms | 0.5213 ms | 0.841x | 1.021x |
| BF16 | 16 | 0.8038 ms | 0.6906 ms | 0.830x | 0.930x |

BF16 per-projection speedups:

| Qwen3.8-27B projection | Rows=1 | Rows=16 | Dense FP16 weight | Packed 4-bit weight |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| full_attn.q_proj | 1.610x | 1.407x | 120.0 MiB | 30.0 MiB |
| full_attn.k_proj | 0.497x | 0.556x | 10.0 MiB | 2.5 MiB |
| full_attn.v_proj | 0.506x | 0.550x | 10.0 MiB | 2.5 MiB |
| full_attn.o_proj | 0.803x | 0.819x | 60.0 MiB | 15.0 MiB |
| linear_attn.in_proj_qkv | 1.385x | 1.301x | 100.0 MiB | 25.0 MiB |
| linear_attn.out_proj | 0.806x | 0.830x | 60.0 MiB | 15.0 MiB |
| mlp.gate_proj | 2.019x | 1.330x | 170.0 MiB | 42.5 MiB |
| mlp.up_proj | 1.962x | 1.351x | 170.0 MiB | 42.5 MiB |
| mlp.down_proj | 0.841x | 0.759x | 170.0 MiB | 42.5 MiB |

The principal end-to-end gain is capacity: 4-bit EXL3 now uses 4x less runtime weight memory than main and avoids model-wide FP16 expansion. The packed path is faster for the important wide BF16 Q/KV/MLP input projections, but narrow outputs and FP16 remain slower than dense MLX. The committed benchmark emits every raw projection/dtype/row result.

## Accuracy

All outputs retain their input activation dtype.

| Coverage | FP16 max abs error | BF16 max abs error |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1–8 bits × 3 codebooks vs dtype-rounded Torch dense decode | 0.0078125 | 0.0625 |
| All 9 Qwen3.8-27B shapes, rows 1/16 vs dtype-rounded Torch oracle | 0.00006103515625 | 0.0000152587890625 |

The all-format maxima are dtype-ULP-scale on random high-magnitude outputs. The Qwen-shape suite validates the packed token and SIMD prefill kernels independently with repeated 128-channel tiles.

## Validation

- `85 passed`: packed conversion/inference accuracy tests, rerun after rebasing onto `6a4379e40`
- `361 passed`: all EXL3 MLX tests
- `3417 passed in 1212.56s`: full `tests/test_mlx_*.py` suite
- Ruff passed locally and in GitHub Actions
- `git diff --check` passed

## Scope and credits

This PR changes only EXL3 inference/conversion plus its tests and benchmark. Changed files retain Apache-2.0 SPDX headers and explicitly credit TurboDerp/ExLlamaV3 (MIT) and Qwen projection shapes (Apache-2.0).

title: Add native MLX GGUF NVFP4 quantization
body:
## Summary

Add the missing native MLX quantization-stage kernel for GGUF NVFP4 on Apple Silicon. The kernel emits the exact 64-value/36-byte GGUF block layout: four UE4M3 scale bytes and 32 packed E2M1 payload bytes.

This PR is intentionally limited to the GGUF NVFP4 weight packer. Connecting GGUF quantization kernels to the model-level processor remains separate follow-up work.

## What Changed

- Added a Metal NVFP4 packer to `gguf_quantize_weight_mlx(..., "NVFP4")`.
- Implemented the GGUF/llama.cpp UE4M3 scale conversion, 16-value subgroups, E2M1 nearest-code selection, saturation, and nibble layout.
- Kept FP16, BF16, and FP32 inputs resident in MLX; non-contiguous inputs are made contiguous by the existing entry point.
- Added an independent Torch oracle, a fixed canonical block-byte vector, random and transposed inputs, runtime decode compatibility, every UE4M3 rounding transition, E2M1 midpoint ±1 ULP checks, saturation, zero, and negative-zero coverage.

- store MLX BitsAndBytes NF4/FP4 kernel results directly in the input activation dtype
- retain FP32 accumulation and preserve the existing decode/prefill thread dispatch

title: Accelerate MLX GPTQ group-16 small BF16 prefill
body:
## Summary

Accelerate MLX GPTQ group-16 small BF16 prefill with a packed Metal row tile for the measured winning envelope. Decode and all unproven/slower prefill shapes retain the existing path.

## What Changed

- Added a packed GPTQ group-16 row-tiled Metal path for 2/3/4/5/6/7/8-bit source formats.
- Dispatch is deliberately limited to BF16, input width >= 5120, output width <= 1024, and row counts 2-8, 12, or 16.
- Kept the prior decode control flow and generated Metal body unchanged.
- Added independent Torch FP64 oracle coverage for FP32 internal arithmetic, visible target-dtype output, boundary-neighbor inputs, bias/no-bias, every bit width, both activation dtypes, all Qwen3.8-27B projections, and native/fallback dispatch.
- Added a reproducible resident-input benchmark.
- No public API changes. Wider outputs, smaller inputs, FP16 prefill, and slower partial-tile row counts remain on the existing path.

## Tests

Every working PR must include at least one new simple, fast, targeted unit test when the change affects behavior, a bug fix, or a regression path.

- [x] Unit tests have been executed and passed, or the reason they are not applicable is documented.
- [x] I added a new simple/fast unit test for this change, or documented why that is not applicable.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. uv run --no-project --with-requirements requirements.txt --with mlx --with torch pytest -q tests/test_mlx_gptq_group16.py
# 433 passed in 23.12s

PYTHONPATH=. uv run --no-project --with-requirements requirements.txt --with mlx --with torch pytest -q tests/test_mlx_gptq_group16.py tests/test_mlx_gptq_output_dtype.py tests/test_mlx_qwen38_native_gptq_audit.py tests/test_mlx_packing.py
# 662 passed in 372.79s

uvx --from ruff==0.14.2 ruff check gptqmodel/nn_modules/qlinear/mlx_gptq.py tests/test_mlx_gptq_group16.py tests/benchmark_mlx_qwen38_gptq_group16_prefill.py
# All checks passed
```

## Review Requirements

AI-assisted code is welcome. The PR must still be reviewed before it is opened as ready for review.

I or an AI agent (such as Codex or Claude) have:

- [x] Reviewed this PR.
- [x] Checked that the code matches existing project structure, APIs, and conventions.
- [x] Avoided unnecessary monkeypatching and used the project's normal extension points where possible.
- [x] Minimized and compacted the impacted code surface.
- [x] Considered and eliminated potential regressions.

## Kernel Accuracy Requirements

- [x] For kernel-related changes, accuracy drift was measured against an applicable independent Torch FP32/FP64 oracle, or the reason this is not applicable is documented.

## Accuracy

Oracle: independently unpacked GPTQ codes and affine parameters evaluated by Torch FP64. FP32 internal arithmetic and visible FP16/BF16 outputs are checked separately at `rtol=atol=2e-3`.

- Native visible outputs changed versus main: **0**
- Native visible/rounded-Torch maximum absolute drift: **0**
- Native FP32/Torch-FP64 maximum absolute drift: **1.1279961e-06**
- Native visible/Torch-FP64 maximum absolute drift: **0.0062206027** (mandatory BF16 output rounding)
- Full matrix visible/rounded maximum: **0.0078125** in unchanged fallback
- Full matrix visible/FP64 maximum: **0.014934072** in unchanged fallback
- Eight unchanged large-output BF16 fallback combinations exceed the broad `2e-3` check by exactly one BF16 output ULP because main rounds two half-matmuls before addition. Tests require exact equality to main, passing FP32-vs-FP64 arithmetic, then explicitly prove the one-ULP bound. This exception is not used for the native path.
- Boundary tests cover neighboring FP16/BF16 values, signed zero, positive/negative inputs, bias/no-bias, all bit widths, and tiled row classes 2/5/8/12/16.

## Performance

Apple Silicon, resident inputs, synchronized `mx.eval`, 10 warmups, 301 interleaved samples, median latency. Rows = 16. All nine Qwen3.8-27B projections, all seven source bit widths, and FP16/BF16 were measured against current main.

- Native minimum speedup: **1.118x**
- Native maximum speedup: **1.196x**
- Decode audit: 126/126 outputs unchanged; median timing ratio **1.000x** against the full prior method.
- Row sweep at the Qwen K/V shape proved every dispatched row class faster across all bit widths. Rows 9-11 and 13-15 were excluded after partial-tile regressions; 2048-output dispatch was excluded after a measured **0.856x** case.

title: Accelerate MLX AWQ group-16 small BF16 prefill
body:
## Summary

Accelerate MLX AWQ group-16 inference for small BF16 prefill batches. The native packed row-tiled kernel is enabled only where it wins on Qwen3.8-27B projection shapes: 2–16 rows and at most 2,048 output features.

## What Changed

- Added a 4-row packed AWQ group-16 prefill tile that accumulates in FP32 and writes BF16 directly.
- Restricted the new dispatch to small-output BF16 prefill; FP16, larger outputs, larger batches, and all decode calls retain the existing main path.
- Kept the existing decode kernel source, launch geometry, and dispatch unchanged after a generalized tiled prototype showed decode regressions.
- Added independent Torch FP64 oracle coverage for boundary inputs and all nine Qwen3.8-27B projection shapes in FP16 and BF16.
- Added a synchronized, interleaved 301-sample benchmark covering all nine projection shapes.
- No public API or serialized-format changes.
- Larger-output prefill optimization is intentionally out of scope because the prototype did not beat main.

## Tests

Every working PR must include at least one new simple, fast, targeted unit test when the change affects behavior, a bug fix, or a regression path.

- [x] Unit tests have been executed and passed, or the reason they are not applicable is documented.
- [x] I added a new simple/fast unit test for this change, or documented why that is not applicable.

Paste the exact test commands and results here:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. uv run --no-project --with-requirements requirements.txt --with mlx --with torch pytest -q tests/test_mlx_awq_group16.py tests/test_mlx_awq_variants.py
# 89 passed in 8.42s

uvx --from ruff==0.14.2 ruff check gptqmodel/nn_modules/qlinear/mlx_awq.py tests/test_mlx_awq_group16.py tests/benchmark_mlx_qwen38_awq_group16_prefill.py
# All checks passed!

python3 -m compileall -q gptqmodel/nn_modules/qlinear/mlx_awq.py tests/test_mlx_awq_group16.py tests/benchmark_mlx_qwen38_awq_group16_prefill.py
git diff --check

PYTHONPATH=. uv run --no-project --with-requirements requirements.txt --with mlx --with torch python tests/benchmark_mlx_qwen38_awq_group16_prefill.py --rows 16 --warmups 10 --samples 301
```

title: Accelerate MLX GGUF Q6_K small BF16 prefill

## Summary

Accelerate GGUF Q6_K BF16 prefill for small-output projections by reusing the existing packed Metal decoder across a four-row tile. On the Qwen3.8-27B K/V projections at 16 rows, the complete layer path is 1.152–1.174× faster than current `main`.

## What Changed

- Generalize the existing packed Q6_K kernel call to multiple row tiles.
- Select one 32-lane SIMD group for the proven small-output BF16 prefill range.

title: Grow dynamic override cache for large MoE models
body:
## Summary

- Size resolved override caches from the larger of physical module paths and GPTQModel's expanded logical MoE plan, with 25% headroom and power-of-two rounding. A fake 120-layer / 512-expert fused shell exercises the logical-path case.
- Keep resolved results with each tracked dynamic configuration. Shared compiled-pattern caches remain global; override keys, first-match behavior, no-match caching, mutation fingerprints, and checkpoint format are unchanged.
- Serialize resolution and tracked mutations with a lock belonging to that configuration. The global lock now covers shared plan-cache access, not PCRE matching, so distinct configs can match in parallel. In-place list operations also advance the mutation version.
- Reserve capacity for the combined working set of live models sharing one dynamic config. Weak model references are pruned on the next cache access, which returns capacity to the remaining live-model bound without a GC callback taking a lock. Explicit manual capacity requests remain grow-only.
- Report cache counters as configuration totals since the caller's snapshot. Two overlapping loads sharing one config can contribute to the same totals.

## Validation

- `python -m pytest tests/qcfg tests/module_tree/test_module_tree_variants.py tests/module_tree/test_moe_tags.py tests/test_looper_helpers.py -q -o log_cli=false`: **142 passed**.
- Ruff and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Three distinct configs enter PCRE matching concurrently in a barrier test. An edit to a shared tracked config waits until an in-flight lookup finishes. Concurrent sizing for two models sharing one config reserves 32,768 entries for two 12K-name working sets, has no traversal evictions, and returns to 16,384 then 8,192 after the models are released.
- The 120-layer / 512-expert fused-MoE regression has fewer than 8,192 physical modules yet sizes for its expanded plan; a second pass over 61,440 expert paths makes zero additional PCRE calls.
- 10K-module / 200 genuine-regex benchmark, winner last: both fixed and adaptive caches make 2,000,000 PCRE calls on the first pass. The fixed cache makes another 2,000,000 on the second; adaptive makes **zero**, with zero evictions (0.129 s versus 0.778 s on this machine).
- Earlier validation of a real Transformers DeepSeek V3 meta shell counted 1,214 physical modules and 48,484 planned logical paths, selecting 65,536 capacity.

Native Python 3.13t / no-GIL execution and a full large-MoE checkpoint load remain unvalidated in this environment. The concurrency tests use barriers and thread interleavings on the available Python 3.12 build.

title: Accelerate MLX EXL3 Hadamard stages

title: Accelerate MLX EXL3 regularization transform
body:
## Summary

Replace the fused EXL3 regularization kernel's dense 128-term Hadamard evaluation with the repository's seven-stage in-threadgroup butterfly transform.

The public API and output shapes/dtypes are unchanged. The change reduces each 128-point vector from 16,384 coefficient FMAs to 896 butterfly additions/subtractions while keeping channel scaling and the transform in one Metal dispatch.

## What Changed

- Reuse two 128-float threadgroup buffers for the normalized Hadamard butterfly.
- Retain the existing input/output channel scaling, zero-channel behavior, and scale outputs.
- Add FP64 adjudication for values where butterfly and Torch dense-matmul reduction order differ.
- Add a targeted cancellation regression and a current-main Qwen3.8-27B benchmark.
- No follow-up work or unrelated quantization methods are included.

Coverage includes small Torch-oracle cases, float32 boundaries, signed/zero channels, skew-policy thresholds, a new FP64 cancellation regression, downstream EXL3 2/4/8-bit codes, and both transform axes for all nine Qwen3.8-27B projections.

## Accuracy

The complete Qwen benchmark compares every output to an independent Torch dense-Hadamard oracle. Output-axis cases stay directly within `rtol=atol=1e-6`. Input-axis reduction order produces 3,468 values outside that direct comparison across 796,917,760 outputs (0.000435%), with maximum absolute Torch drift `4.29153442e-6`; maximum normalized drift is `2.17446825e-7`, and maximum scale drift is exactly `0`.

Those outliers are not accepted by a blanket tolerance. The tests recompute each outlier from the stored float32 scaled inputs using an independent float64 Hadamard row/column and require the butterfly result to be within `rtol=atol=1e-6` and no farther from FP64 than Torch. All outliers pass. On the full Qwen K input projection, maximum butterfly error versus FP64 is `8.53971528e-7` with normalized error `8.25177574e-8`, versus Torch's `3.45479022e-6` and `2.05758038e-7`.

title: Reduce MLX MXFP4 codebook search
body:
## Summary

Reduce the native MLX GGUF MXFP4 nearest-code search from all 16 signed codebook entries to the eight nonnegative magnitudes. The kernel applies the source sign after selecting the magnitude, preserving the existing lower-magnitude tie rule and packed bytes while removing seven impossible opposite-sign comparisons per weight.

title: Accelerate MLX BitsAndBytes subnormal quantization
body:
## Summary

Make the all-subnormal FP32 BitsAndBytes NF4/FP4 path native to MLX and correct at quantization boundaries.

The existing fallback copied block maxima to NumPy, looped on the CPU, and used an approximate 16-bit lookup. Its packer also used one fixed reciprocal for every subnormal block. This PR selects a dedicated subnormal Metal packer, computes nested statistics in integer mantissa space, and binary-searches the exact float32 codebook boundaries. Ordinary FP16/BF16 and normal FP32 inputs continue through the unchanged existing pack kernel.

## What Changed

- Added a dedicated Metal packer for all-subnormal FP32 NF4/FP4 blocks.
- Replaced the NumPy/CPU nested-statistics fallback with MLX uint64/int64 reductions and a Metal codebook search.
- Preserved round-to-nearest-ties-to-even for the exact subnormal offset.
- Kept the common normal-value pack kernel unchanged after a regression sweep showed that an in-kernel branch cost about 4%.
- Added Torch A/B boundary coverage, an independent FP64 nested-statistics oracle, and a reproducible nine-shape benchmark.
- No public API or checkpoint-layout change.

## Accuracy

The independent oracle treats each float32 subnormal as its exact integer mantissa times the common subnormal unit, computes the offset with exact ties-to-even rounding, and compares rational values directly with the stored float32 codebook boundaries.

Main differs because the prior fixed reciprocal and approximate nested lookup select incorrect discrete codes. The PR has zero mismatches and zero float drift against the FP64 oracle on every Qwen3.8-27B projection and both formats:

title: Avoid FP32 temporaries in MLX FP8 quantization

title: Vectorize MLX ParoQuant rotation metadata

## Summary

- Add a reproducible current-main-vs-vectorized benchmark for all nine required projection shapes.

title: Avoid FP32 temporaries in MLX RTN quantization
body:
## Summary

Optimize native MLX RTN quantization by passing contiguous FP16, BF16, and FP32 weights directly to the existing group parallel Metal kernel instead of materializing a full FP32 weight copy.

Each weight load is converted explicitly to FP32 inside the kernel. Min/max reduction, scale and zero-point calculation, code rounding, and dequantization therefore retain the existing FP32 arithmetic. The returned dequantized weight still preserves the source FP16/BF16 dtype.

This PR is intentionally limited to RTN.

## Accuracy coverage

The focused RTN suite covers:

- every supported bit rate: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 bits
- group sizes `-1`, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, and 1024
- symmetric and asymmetric quantization
- FP16 and BF16 inputs
- all nine Qwen3.8-27B projection shapes
- rounding, zero-point, endpoint, and transposed-storage regressions
- Torch oracle comparison for dequantized weights, scales, zero points, and group indices

The performance audit compares all four returned tensors against main. Maximum error is zero in every row.

- keep resident FP16, BF16, and FP32 TQ2_0 inputs in their original dtype instead of allocating a full-tensor FP32 temporary

title: Sync GGUF Q8_1 block size with llama.cpp
body:
## Summary

- correct the vendored GGUF Q8_1 block size from 40 bytes to 36 bytes
- match llama.cpp's `block_q8_1` C ABI: two FP16 values plus 32 int8 quants
- add a minimal GGUF reader regression fixture that verifies the 36-byte payload exactly
- add SPDX and llama.cpp GGUF credit headers to every changed file

## Upstream audit

Latest stable Python package: `gguf==0.19.0` (May 6, 2026).

GPTQModel already vendors the 0.19.0 reader API and supplies its own quantizers, so this PR does not add an external `gguf` dependency. Adding one would make packing behavior depend on whether the optional package is installed.

The 0.19.0 Python size table still describes Q8_1 as 40 bytes, while the llama.cpp C ABI at that release is 36 bytes. Current llama.cpp `master` corrects the Python table to `2 + 2 + 32`. Its only new quantization enum since 0.19.0 is Q2_0, which GPTQModel already supports. Stable 0.19.0 also added NVFP4 dequantization, which GPTQModel already supports.

Sources:

- https://pypi.org/project/gguf/
- https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/gguf-v0.19.0/ggml/src/ggml-common.h
- https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/gguf-py/gguf/constants.py

## Compatibility impact

| Item | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Q8_1 logical block | 32 values | 32 values |
| Reader bytes per block | 40 | 36 |
| llama.cpp C ABI match | No | Yes |

This is a reader metadata correction. It does not change inference, quantization, or MLX kernels, so kernel speed metrics are not applicable.

title: Add native MLX EXL3 Hessian finalization
body:
## Summary

Add an opt-in native MLX finalizer for EXL3 calibration Hessians. The complete path performs sample averaging, diagonal regularization, input-sign application, the two-sided order-128 Hadamard transform, fallback detection, block-LDL factorization, and scalar-diagonal clearing without routing tensors through Torch.

The two transform passes fuse averaging, regularization, and sign application. Their two `1/sqrt(128)` factors are applied once as the exactly representable combined factor `1/128`, reducing memory traffic and intermediate rounding.

## What Changed

- Added `exl3_finalize_hessian_mlx` for accumulated float32 Hessians and caller-supplied deterministic signs.
- Added explicit validation for shapes, dtypes, finite inputs, signs, sample counts, regularization, block sizes, and the Metal kernel's 32-bit index boundary.
- Added intended empty-capture fallback behavior and representable-neighbor tests around EXL3's `1e-20` fallback threshold.
- Added an independent Torch float32 oracle and a Torch float64 adjudication oracle, including EXL3's explicit identity-block overwrite before scalar-diagonal clearing.
- Added all nine Qwen3.8-27B projection checks and a resident-input benchmark.
- Kept processor integration and RNG/sign generation out of scope so this remains one focused EXL3 quantization-stage PR.

## Accuracy

The oracle starts from the same stored float32 accumulated Hessian and deterministic seeded pseudo-random signs. Matrix results are checked over the complete output with `atol=rtol=1e-6`, normalized drift `||actual-reference||/||reference|| <= 1e-6`, and explicit nonfinite counts. The table uses the independent Torch float64 path as the reference.

Both float32 backends remain within the normalized limit on the realistic sign pattern. MLX's zero-diagonal factor is closer to the higher-precision reference on every Qwen width: at most `6.25e-7` normalized drift versus Torch's `8.22e-7`.

title: Add native MLX EXL3 sign packing
body:
## Summary

- add an opt-in native MLX Metal packer for EXL3's compact `su`/`sv` sign tensors
- pack 16 sign bits into each little-endian int16 word, matching EXL3's CUDA format
- support float16, float32, and bfloat16 resident MLX inputs without materializing EXL3's intermediate float16 cast
- preserve signed zero, underflow/overflow signs, infinities, and positive/negative NaN sign bits
- validate dtype, nonempty inputs, and 16-value packing boundaries
- keep this PR limited to EXL3 sign packing; it does not change current `suh`/`svh` checkpoint emission

The EXL3 loader still supports compact packed `su` and `sv` tensors. Main's packer is a CUDA extension and cannot run on M chips; this supplies the native resident-data MLX path.

## Accuracy

Target: Mac Studio, M5 Ultra, 256 GB. Qwen checks use resident bfloat16 signs and compare every packed int16 word with an independent Torch oracle. Sign packing is discrete, so acceptance is exact equality rather than a floating tolerance.

title: Add native MLX EXL3 block-LDL factorization
body:
## Summary

- add an opt-in native MLX implementation of EXL3's block-LDL Hessian factorization
- use MLX's supported CPU-stream Cholesky and batched triangular inverse
- fuse the dense block-column normalization into a Metal float32-FMA kernel
- write exact identity diagonal blocks and preserve the source algorithm's block-unit-lower layout
- reject nonfinite inputs, singular/non-positive-definite Hessians, invalid block sizes, nonfinite inverses, and nonfinite outputs
- keep this PR limited to block-LDL; LDLQ remains the separate merged PR #3172

MLX 0.32.2 does not expose Cholesky on the GPU. This implementation therefore keeps factorization on MLX's native CPU stream and moves the bandwidth-heavy normalization to Metal.

## Accuracy

Target: Mac Studio, M5 Ultra, 256 GB. Tests use block size 16 and a dense positive-definite AR(1) Hessian with correlation 0.2. The factorization depends only on input width, so repeated projection rows reuse the measured 5,120 or 6,144 result. Every full factor is compared with an independent Torch oracle using `atol=1e-6`, `rtol=1e-6`, normalized drift no greater than `1e-6`, and an explicit nonfinite check.

| Projection | Checkpoint shape | Hessian shape | Outside tolerance | Max abs drift | Normalized drift | Nonfinite |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| full_attn.q_proj | 12288×5120 | 5120×5120 | 0 | 4.17232526e-10 | 1.06789868e-10 | 0 |
| full_attn.k_proj | 1024×5120 | 5120×5120 | 0 | 4.17232526e-10 | 1.06789868e-10 | 0 |
| full_attn.v_proj | 1024×5120 | 5120×5120 | 0 | 4.17232526e-10 | 1.06789868e-10 | 0 |

| mlp.down_proj | 5120×17408 | 17408×17408 | 0 | 4.17232526e-10 | 1.06907648e-10 | 0 |

Additional numerical coverage:

- float64 Torch oracle on a dense random SPD Hessian
- float32 Torch oracle for block sizes 8, 16, and 32
- normalization values immediately below, at, and above float32 boundaries, including signed zero and the smallest positive subnormal
- positive-definite boundary at `nextafter(1, 0)`, with exact singular and just-indefinite matrices rejected
- NaN and positive/negative infinity rejected before factorization

## Performance

title: Add native MLX EXL3 LDLQ quantization
body:
## Summary

- add an opt-in native MLX implementation of EXL3's Hessian-compensated LDLQ stage
- preserve EXL3's descending 16-row block order and buffered error-feedback semantics
- reuse the existing native MLX EXL3 tile-layout and Viterbi kernels
- add a dedicated Metal float32-FMA reduction for `factor.T @ error`
- retain compensation only for the unquantized prefix to avoid writes that cannot be consumed
- keep this PR limited to LDLQ; it does not integrate unrelated EXL3 stages

The generic MLX matmul path was not accepted blindly: on a dense feedback fixture its normalized correction drift was `5.9159965e-6`, it crossed 69 float16 input boundaries, and it ultimately changed 57 trellis states. The dedicated reduction removes that regression.

## Accuracy

Target: Mac Studio, M5 Ultra, 256 GB. EXL3 matrix layout is `(input_features, output_features)`. Qwen tests use 4-bit MCG and a nonzero `2^-16` block-subdiagonal LDL coupling. Every complete reconstructed weight and every unpacked trellis state is compared with an independent Torch oracle.

## Summary

Add a standalone native MLX path for EXL3 fallback quantization when no usable Hessian/LDL decomposition is available. It composes the merged tensor-core tile transform, native Viterbi quantizer, and inverse transform while preserving the existing EXL3 output layout.

This PR covers the fallback branch only. LDLQ compensation, processor integration, regularization, and packing changes are intentionally out of scope.

## What Changed

- Added `exl3_fallback_quantize_mlx(...)` for regularized EXL3 float32 weights.
- Returns the reconstructed float32 matrix plus unpacked int16 trellis states in the same shapes as the Torch/CUDA path.

## Summary

Add native MLX orchestration for EXL3 global-scale search. The new API combines the merged wrapped-diagonal sampler and native Viterbi quantizer with EXL3's fixed golden-section search and float32 MSE calculation.

This PR is limited to the global-scale-search stage. Processor integration, regularization changes, Viterbi changes, and LDLQ remain out of scope.

## What Changed

- Added `exl3_global_scale_search_mlx(...)` with EXL3's `[0.1, 1.9]` interval and `0.01` stopping tolerance.
- Preserved float32 MSE/final-average semantics and Python-double interval arithmetic from the Torch path.
- Added an independent Torch oracle that performs its own Viterbi search and golden-section control flow.
- Added bits 2/4/8, all-codebook, rounding-boundary, validation, and all nine Qwen3.8-27B projection tests.
- Updated the reproducible Qwen benchmark to report exact selected-scale, absolute-MSE, and relative-MSE drift.

## Accuracy

Environment: Apple M5 Ultra (256 GB), MLX 0.32.2, Torch 2.14.0. Tests use full Qwen matrix dimensions with a deterministic four-tile pattern bank. The independent Torch oracle quantizes each unique tile itself, expands the results back over every sampled tile, and computes MSE over the complete sampled output.

title: Add native MLX GGUF Q6_K decode kernel

## Summary

- add `MlxGGUFQ6KLinear`, a GGUF Q6_K runtime that inherits `MlxGroup16Linear` and keeps the existing validated packed parameter layout

title: Add fused MLX EXL3 regularization kernel
body:
## Summary

- add one fused native MLX Metal kernel for EXL3 channel scaling plus the immediately following normalized 128-point Hadamard transform
- support output regularization (output RMS normalization/signs followed by the right transform) and input regularization (input RMS/codebook scaling followed by the left transform)
- emit the stored `sv`/`su` scale vectors in the same pass
- keep the API standalone and opt-in; this PR does not change EXL3 processor orchestration
- add independent Torch-oracle, threshold/boundary, zero-scale, invalid-input, and complete Qwen3.8-27B coverage

This replaces two full matrix passes with one kernel. RMS calculation, global-scale search, LDLQ, Viterbi search, and packing remain separate stages.

## Numerical design

An initial seven-stage butterfly was faster but not accepted blindly: realistic post-input-scale Qwen data produced 446 of 62,914,560 values outside `atol=rtol=1e-6`, with maximum absolute drift `2.861023e-6`. Pre-normalizing before the butterfly was also tested and was slightly worse.

The submitted kernel instead evaluates each normalized Sylvester-128 dot product directly from shared memory with FMA. This matches main's dense Torch Hadamard arithmetic exactly on every tested Qwen value while retaining a substantial speedup.

## Accuracy and performance versus main

Oracle/baseline: independent Torch float32 channel-scale arithmetic followed by main's blockwise dense Torch Hadamard transform. Complete transformed matrices and complete stored scale vectors are compared with combined `atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-6` and normalized RMS drift at most `1e-6`.

title: Add native MLX EXL3 Viterbi quantization kernel
body:
## Summary

- add a native MLX/Metal implementation of EXL3's two-pass tail-biting Viterbi tile quantizer
- support every EXL3 bit width (1–8) and all three codebooks (`3inst`, `mcg`, and `mul1`)
- preserve the canonical FP32-to-FP16 input conversion, fused FP16 cost accumulation, strict tie ordering, cyclic backtrace, unpacked int16 states, and FP32 reconstructed values
- bound scratch memory independently of projection size by reusing a fixed set of Viterbi workspace slots

This PR is intentionally limited to EXL3 path search/tile quantization. Codebook reconstruction and trellis packing were merged separately, and this does not wire the opt-in MLX primitive into the CUDA/HIP-only EXL3 processor.

## Accuracy

The independent Torch oracle implements the state graph and arithmetic separately. In particular, it models the CUDA/Metal fused `delta² + prior_cost` operation with one FP16 rounding; it does not call or reuse MLX intermediates.

Coverage includes:

- exact unpacked int16 states and reconstructed values for bits 1–8
- exact outputs for `3inst`, `mcg`, and `mul1`
- representable FP16 tie boundaries plus one FP16 step below and above
- positive/negative values, signed zero, codebook extrema, and forced one-slot workspace reuse
- complete outputs for every Qwen3.8-27B projection shape

The model-scale tests repeat a deterministic four-tile random bank to each full projection tile count. Every output element is checked; the repeated bank keeps the independent CPU oracle tractable without reducing the MLX workload.

| Projection | Shape | Tiles | Values checked | Index mismatches | Value mismatches | Max abs drift |

| full_attn.q_proj | 12288×5120 | 245,760 | 62,914,560 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

## Performance

The resident Torch oracle is prohibitively slow at full projection scale, so its median four-tile runtime is linearly extrapolated to each tile count. The speedup column is therefore an estimate, not a directly measured end-to-end Torch or CUDA comparison.

title: Add native MLX EXL3 codebook reconstruction kernel
body:
## Summary

- add an MLX-native EXL3 codebook reconstruction kernel for the `3inst`, `mcg`, and `mul1` codebooks
- preserve signed `int16` state bit patterns and reproduce EXL3 half-precision arithmetic before returning FP32 values
- add an independent Torch oracle, exhaustive state-space coverage, Qwen3.8-27B projection-shape regression tests, and a reproducible benchmark

This PR is intentionally limited to EXL3 codebook reconstruction. It does not add or modify the Viterbi/path-search stage.

## Accuracy

The independent Torch oracle does not import or call the MLX implementation.

- all 65,536 encoded states checked for each of the three codebooks
- signed-state boundaries checked explicitly
- all nine Qwen3.8-27B projection outputs checked element-by-element
- exact agreement: zero mismatched values and zero absolute drift

title: Add native MLX EXL3 trellis packing kernel
body:
## Summary

Add a native MLX Metal kernel for EXL3 trellis packing on Apple silicon.

This PR is intentionally limited to one EXL3 quantization-finalization stage: converting the quantizer's 256-state int16 tiles into EXL3's checkpoint trellis words. It does not add EXL3 codebook search, Hessian processing, or optimizer integration.

## What Changed

- Added `exl3_pack_trellis_mlx` for EXL3 bit widths 1–8.
- Preserved EXL3's exact logical big-endian bitstream and adjacent uint16 swap used by its checkpoint layout.
- Added strict shape, dtype, nonempty-tile, and bit-width validation.
- Added an independent Torch arithmetic oracle that does not call or reuse the MLX kernel.
- Added exact boundary coverage for signed int16 state limits, low-bit mask endpoints, and values immediately across the mask boundary for every supported bit width.
- Added save/load and bits 1–8 roundtrips through the existing `ExllamaV3TorchLinear` decoder.
- Added exact complete-output checks and benchmarks for every Qwen3.8-27B projection shape.
- Follow-up intentionally out of scope: native MLX EXL3 Viterbi/codebook search and Hessian-driven optimization.

## Accuracy and Performance

Measured on Apple M5 Ultra, 256 GB, MLX 0.32.2, Torch 2.14.0. Qwen checks use EXL3's default 3-bit trellis layout. Inputs are already resident; timings are medians of three measured calls after one warmup.

Main's production `pack_trellis` implementation is CUDA-only and cannot execute on Apple silicon. Therefore the comparison below is against an independent exact Torch implementation of the same main-format bit-packing algorithm, not against CUDA timing. Packed int16 words are discrete format data and must match exactly.

| Projection | Weight shape | Packed words | Mismatched words | Max word drift | Torch ms | MLX ms | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| full_attn.q_proj | 12288×5120 | 11,796,480 | 0 | 0 | 401.046 | 0.853 | 470.07× |
| full_attn.k_proj | 1024×5120 | 983,040 | 0 | 0 | 34.224 | 0.258 | 132.54× |
| full_attn.v_proj | 1024×5120 | 983,040 | 0 | 0 | 34.177 | 0.228 | 150.01× |
| full_attn.o_proj | 5120×6144 | 5,898,240 | 0 | 0 | 204.355 | 0.525 | 388.97× |
| linear_attn.in_proj_qkv | 10240×5120 | 9,830,400 | 0 | 0 | 334.260 | 0.798 | 418.78× |
| linear_attn.out_proj | 5120×6144 | 5,898,240 | 0 | 0 | 201.028 | 0.543 | 369.99× |
| mlp.gate_proj | 17408×5120 | 16,711,680 | 0 | 0 | 578.132 | 1.084 | 533.31× |

| mlp.down_proj | 5120×17408 | 16,711,680 | 0 | 0 | 573.291 | 1.302 | 440.44× |

title: Add native MLX ParoQuant rotation kernel
body:
## Summary

Add a native MLX Metal kernel for ParoQuant's calibration-time grouped Givens rotation stage on Apple silicon.

The new standalone primitive supports forward transformed-weight rotation and the inverse transform used to map export-domain weights back to input space. It keeps FP32 intermediates, validates pair schedules and finite/value boundaries, and is intentionally not wired into ParoQuant's Torch autograd optimizer in this PR.

## What Changed

- Added `paroquant_rotate_mlx` for rank-2+ FP16, BF16, and FP32 weights.
- Added grouped forward and inverse rotations for group sizes 16, 32, 64, and 128, with optional positive channel scales.
- Added explicit shape, dtype, finite-value, positive-scale, and local pair-permutation validation.
- Added an independent Torch arithmetic oracle covering:
  - FP16, BF16, and FP32 inputs
  - forward and inverse transforms
  - exact zero and quarter-turn angles plus one representable FP32 step on each side
  - rank-3 inputs and the no-channel-scale path
  - every Qwen3.8-27B Q/K/V/O, fused QKV/O, and MLP gate/up/down weight shape
  - quantize → pack → save/load compatibility with the merged ParoQuant MLX path
- Added a reproducible per-shape benchmark against `main`'s Torch ParoQuant rotation path.
- Follow-up intentionally out of scope: replacing the Torch autograd optimization loop. This PR is one method-stage/kernel only.

## Accuracy and Performance

Measured on Apple M5 Ultra, 256 GB, MLX 0.32.2, Torch 2.14.0. Inputs use Qwen3.8-27B BF16 weights, eight ParoQuant rotation stages, group size 128, and resident weight/theta/scale tensors. title: Add staged GSQ training and public method adapters
body:
## Summary

- Add opt-in staged scalar GSQ for dense Llama GPTQ W2/W3/W4 and AWQ W4. The training schedule fits Q/K separately with projected-Hessian objectives, V/O jointly against attention output, and the MLP projections jointly against block output. Completed packed blocks feed the next block's calibration capture.
- Train discrete assignments and group scales with Gumbel-Softmax, Lion or AdamW, temperature/logit schedules, and GPTQ, RTN, or AWQ initializers. Export through existing GPTQ_V2 or AWQ GEMM checkpoints.
- Extend local GSQ refinement to compatible AWQ, RTN, QQQ, FP8, and ParoQuant paths. Add calibrated FP8 refinement, exact AWQ packing-code checks, and explicit QQQ Torch backend selection.
- Document supported methods, formats, constraints, and GSQ attribution in the README. New files carry ModelCloud/qubitium SPDX headers.

## Validation

- `93 passed, 33 skipped` across scalar GSQ, staged training, method adapters, weight-only configuration, format conversion, and NPU support tests. The staged tests exercise all seven projections per block and exact GPTQ/AWQ save-load logits on tiny Llama models. QQQ Torch save-load is covered on CPU without the optional native extension.
- Llama 3.2 1B Instruct, 32 nm-calibration records concatenated to six 2,048-token sequences, W4/group128, all 16 decoder blocks, 128 GSM8K Platinum rows, 96 generated tokens, seed 898:

| Recipe | Quantization time after setup | GSM8K Platinum |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Staged path, GPTQ initializer only | 69.0 s | 36/128 (28.1%) |
| Staged GSQ, one epoch and one Q/K step | 152.1 s | 31/128 (24.2%) |
| Staged GSQ, two epochs and two Q/K steps | 190.9 s | 28/128 (21.9%) |

These short schedules regress on this quality check. They are functional smoke tests, not evidence of a quality gain. The paper uses a much larger training budget. The opt-in 1B test records these observations and enforces a configurable minimum score.

The expanded quality recipe uses the first 128 nm-calibration records (25 concatenated 2,048-token sequences), 10 epochs, and 10 Q/K steps. The same 128 GSM8K Platinum rows and generation settings were used for both checkpoints:

| 128-record recipe | Quantization time after setup | GSM8K Platinum |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Staged path, GPTQ initializer only | 137.3 s | 40/128 (31.3%) |
| Staged GSQ, 10 epochs and 10 Q/K steps | Not separated by this test | 34/128 (26.6%) |

The W4 GSQ score above was measured **before** the dense-attention teacher correction in `e3db0e4`. It regressed by 6/128 against its matched initializer under the earlier objective; W4 must be remeasured for the current code. The corrected objective now targets original dense attention outputs for V/O and the complete block for MLP, matching the public reference trainer. The local parquet fixture reads only the selected rows, avoiding a full 10,000-record load. The 32-record scores above are historical and should not be compared directly with this recipe.

With the corrected objective, the same 128-record recipe was retested at **W3/group128** across all 16 blocks and all seven projections, including packed save/reload. Both checkpoints used the same 128 GSM8K Platinum rows, seed 898, and 96 generated tokens:

| W3 128-record recipe | Quantization time after setup | GSM8K Platinum |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Staged path, GPTQ initializer only | 139.6 s | 6/128 (4.7%) |
| Staged GSQ, 10 epochs and 10 Q/K steps | Not separated by this test | 2/128 (1.6%) |

Staged GSQ regressed by **4/128** (3.1 percentage points) on this W3 check. The test set `GPTQMODEL_GSQ_STAGED_MIN_GSM8K=0` to measure the score; both W3 checkpoints fail the normal 20% quality gate. This is a single small-sample result and does not establish the cause. The W3 result is not comparable with the historical W4 score because both precision and the teacher objective differ. The W3 checkpoint loaded and evaluated, and five tiny GPTQ/RTN/AWQ checkpoint roundtrip tests passed. The PR remains draft pending quality work.

## Comparison with the GSQ paper

- The W3 scalar grid, five local shifts, trainable group scales, Gumbel-Softmax relaxation, Lion optimizer, annealing endpoints, and Q/K → V/O → MLP stage order follow the paper and its [public reference implementation](https://github.com/IST-DASLab/GSQ). The dense-attention teacher objective was corrected in `e3db0e4`; five tiny GPTQ/RTN/AWQ checkpoint tests pass after the change.
- The paper's Llama experiment uses FineWeb-Edu, 4,096 sequences of length 4,096, 20 epochs, and optimizer batches of 64. This Llama 3.2 1B quality test uses nm-calibration, 25 sequences of length 2,048, 10 epochs, and batches of 1: roughly 655 times fewer training token exposures. Its microbatch is also 1, so it does not average gradients across independent Gumbel draws as in the paper's accumulation recipe. Its Q/K schedule is 10 updates versus 2,000 in the reference code. The public reference separates GPTQ, training, and validation samples; this test reuses the 25 sequences for GPTQ and training and has no held-out validation stage.
- The [paper's Equation 6](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.18556) describes clipping shifts at grid boundaries; both the released integer quantizer and this port mask out-of-grid shifts. This is a paper-versus-code detail, separate from the test-budget differences.
- The paper evaluates Llama 3.1 8B/70B on five zero-shot tasks; this PR tests Llama 3.2 1B on 128 GSM8K Platinum questions. The paper's optional full-model scale-only pass is for 2-bit Llama and is not implemented here. Its ternary, GGUF, mixed-bit, and MoE training paths are outside this public dense-Llama staged path.

## Limits

- Staged training currently targets dense Llama blocks, one materialized device, eager or SDPA attention, and the listed GPTQ/AWQ formats. The paper's optional end-to-end scale-only pass for 2-bit Llama is not included.
- Full 1B AWQ training was attempted but stopped after over 22 minutes in the existing block-2 GPU-to-CPU calibration feature capture. Tiny AWQ all-projection training and exact save-load were validated.
- The native QQQ CUDA extension could not be exercised on this host because the CUDA toolkit is absent. Its Torch backend and packed checkpoint path were validated.

## Current W3 paper-budget recipe (NM source)

The new opt-in `tests/models/test_llama3_2_gsq_paper_w3.py` uses Llama 3.2 1B Instruct, W3/group128, all 16 blocks and all seven projections. It matches the paper's Llama data geometry: **4,096 training**, **128 validation**, and **512 GPTQ initialization** sequences, each **4,096 tokens** (19,398,656 tokens total). It also uses **20 epochs**, batch **64**, microbatch **2**, **2,000 Q/K updates**, and the Llama Lion learning rates, weight decay, annealing, and cosine schedule. GPTQ initialization and late MLP reinitialization now use the separate GPTQ split, and V/O plus MLP stages record held-out validation loss.

The full [FineWeb-Edu dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/HuggingFaceFW/fineweb-edu) is about **5.84 TB**, and the [sample/10BT](https://huggingface.co/datasets/HuggingFaceFW/fineweb-edu/tree/main/sample/10BT) is **28.5 GB**, so this recipe uses the existing 12.8 MB `nm-calibration/llm.parquet` instead. Its 10,000 source rows are shuffled and partitioned before repetition. Each split repeats only its own rows to reach the target tokens; unique text diversity remains about six times smaller than the paper's. Source SHA256 and exact counts are in `docs/experiments/gsq-paper-budget-1b-w3.md`. The model and 128-question GSM8K Platinum evaluation differ from the paper's Llama 3.1 8B/70B and five zero-shot benchmarks.

The public Llama module tree now carries explicit `q`, `k`, `v`, `o`, `gate`, `up`, and `down` roles while preserving shared-input tags and projection subsets. The staged trainer selects the seven projections by name, so these tags do not change the GSQ objective.

**Validation:** 245 focused tests passed; 2 full-budget E2E parametrizations were skipped by default. The real NM tokenizer produced the exact 4,096/128/512 sequences of length 4,096. Dense Llama 3.2 1B scored **54/128 (42.2%)** on the same GSM8K settings. The single-block, full-length GPU smoke passed with batch 64, microbatch 2, finite V/O and MLP validation losses, and cleaned disk capture (21.6 seconds for block quantization after data preparation). The 512-sequence, all-block W3 initializer completed, saved, and reloaded. It scored **5/128 (3.9%)** on GSM8K Platinum, versus **54/128 (42.2%)** for dense Llama 3.2 1B. The prior opt-in test failed solely because the 20% quality threshold was applied to this reference baseline; the threshold now applies only to GSQ. The complete 20-epoch W3 GSQ quantization and resulting GSM8K score have **not been measured**. This PR stays draft pending that quality result.

## Attribution

The staged training and scalar refinement are adapted from [GSQ by Dadgarnia et al. (IST-DASLab)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.18556) and its [public reference implementation](https://github.com/IST-DASLab/GSQ).

## Training speed update (commit `0b146b4`)

The attempted 20-epoch W3 run was stopped during block 1, MLP update 436/1,280, because the original training path was too slow. No completed GSQ checkpoint or GSM8K score exists from that run; the temporary 75 GB activation capture was removed.

A CUDA NVRTC fused scalar relaxation now covers W3/W4 BF16 MLP/V/O logits and FP32 Q/K logits, with any positive contiguous group size. Unsupported CUDA setups and CPU use the eager path. Fixed dense-teacher outputs and MLP residuals are cached at the original microbatch geometry for disk-backed SDPA Llama training; the next MLP optimizer batch is prefetched. The caches are removed after each stage. CUDA and eager use the same equations, with small floating-point rounding differences in the CUDA kernels. Numerical forward/gradient comparisons and 59 focused tests passed, followed by 8 CUDA-specific tests after adding the nonstandard group-size case; the opt-in full quality check remains unmeasured.

On 128 captured Llama 3.2 1B W3/group128 documents of 4,096 tokens, batch 64, microbatch 2, two optimizer batches per trial:

| Stage | Eager | Optimized | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| MLP, trial 1 | 18.34 s | 4.41 s | 4.16× |
| MLP, trial 2 | 19.08 s | 4.49 s | 4.25× |
| V/O attention, trial 1 | 3.54 s | 1.98 s | 1.79× |
| V/O attention, trial 2 | 3.36 s | 1.91 s | 1.76× |

A separate warmed 2,048×2,048 FP32-logit Q/K update with its quadratic loss took about 33 ms eager versus 13 ms fused (2.5×). The MLP and V/O measurements sum to roughly **3.4–3.5×**, so a **4× end-to-end speedup is not established**. Cache construction took 10.4 s for MLP and 2.0 s for attention on those 128 documents; these and GPTQ initialization, hard validation, packing, and generation are excluded from the table. Full-data MLP target caching temporarily requires roughly 128 GiB of disk, with separate stage caches cleaned on exit. Reproduction details and limitations are in `docs/experiments/gsq-paper-budget-1b-w3.md`.

## CUDA precision follow-up (`8834d8b`)

A targeted audit found a precision error in the first fused Q/K kernel: it stored FP32 softmax probabilities as BF16 and rounded W3/W4 scalar shifts before adding them to the FP32 initializer. Both are corrected. A crafted low-temperature test now checks that a nearly certain choice retains its small, nonzero FP32 gradient.

The updated focused suite passed **66 tests**. Three 30-update matched-randomness trajectories covered W3 BF16, W4 BF16, and W3 FP32, comparing hard choices and reconstruction loss. A paired three-epoch tiny Llama W3 run trained and packed all seven projections; eager and CUDA yielded identical packed-model logits and measured hard-stage losses in that case. In a separate synthetic 2,048×2,048 W3/group128 Q/K probe, the corrected kernel had no gradient-sign disagreements with eager among 20,971,520 logits at each of four sampled schedule points, including temperature 0.05 / multiplier 500. This does not establish full 1B model quality.

With the corrected kernel and isolated GPU measurements, the three-projection MLP relaxation measured **206.9 ms eager versus 25.8 ms fused** per microbatch (8.0× for this suboperation). A warmed 2,048×2,048 FP32 Q/K update measured about **33.5 ms eager versus 13.7 ms fused** (2.4×). The earlier stage timings above used the first kernel version; corrected-kernel timings are below. The stopped 20-epoch W3 GSM8K evaluation remains unmeasured; the PR stays draft.

## Corrected-kernel stage timing (`a1abd20`)

The two-stage timing was repeated after the FP32 precision correction with Llama 3.2 1B layer dimensions, W3/group128, 4,096 tokens, batch 64, microbatch 2, and 128 synthetic captured documents. Both paths used the same inputs and two optimizer batches. The synthetic source was repeated random BF16 activation data; this is a shape-matched speed test, not a quality result.

| Stage | Eager, trials 1 / 2 | Optimized, trials 1 / 2 | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| MLP | 18.08 / 18.11 s | 4.39 / 4.40 s | 4.11–4.12× |
| V/O attention | 3.51 / 3.39 s | 1.93 / 1.91 s | 1.77–1.82× |
| Sum of measured stages | 21.59 / 21.50 s | 6.32 / 6.30 s | 3.41× |

MLP cache setup took 7.60 s; attention cache setup took 2.06 s for 128 documents. These setup costs, Q/K training, GPTQ initialization, validation, packing, and evaluation are outside the table. Attention batch prefetch was tested and gave no reliable improvement, so it was omitted. The full 20-epoch W3 quality run remains stopped and unmeasured. See `docs/experiments/gsq-paper-budget-1b-w3.md` for method and limits.

title: Add native MLX ParoQuant pseudo-quantization kernel
body:
## Summary

Add a fused MLX Metal kernel for ParoQuant's transformed-weight pseudo-quantization. It applies learned float32 scales and optional affine zero-point parameters, rounds ties to even, clamps the codes, dequantizes, and returns the original weight dtype.

## What Changed

- Add `paroquant_quantize_weight_mlx` in `gptqmodel/quantization/mlx_paroquant_quant.py`.
- Accept both grouped qparams `(out_features, groups)` and the flattened layout used by `GroupLinearQuantizer`.
- Add an independent Torch reference, exact rounding-boundary tests for 2–8 bits, FP32/FP16/BF16 input coverage, and Qwen3.8-27B shape coverage for symmetric and affine quantization.
- Add resident-input performance measurements against the non-STE Torch pseudo-quantization arithmetic.

title: Require FP16 and BF16 accuracy checks for MLX kernels

title: Add native MLX QQQ quantization kernel

## Summary

Add an opt-in native MLX Metal kernel for QQQ 4-bit weight quantization. It supports QQQ's signed `group_size=-1` format and dynamic symmetric `group_size=128` format, including sequential inverse-Hessian error updates and the per-row int8 scale output for grouped QQQ.

## What Changed

- Add `qqq_quantize_weight_mlx` in `gptqmodel/quantization/mlx_qqq.py`. Inputs use the existing QQQ upper inverse-Hessian factor and preordered weight layout. Outputs are pseudo-quantized weights and QQQ metadata; QQQ inference packing and activation ordering remain outside this primitive.
- Add an independent Torch oracle, rounding-boundary and dtype-cast cases, and Qwen3.8-27B projection tests for both group modes.
- Add a per-shape resident-input benchmark.

## Numerical Validation

The Qwen tests use BF16 weights and an independently generated Torch reference with a unit diagonal and 0.05 superdiagonal inverse-Hessian factor. title: Preserve ParoQuant MLX activation output dtype
body:
## Scope

ParoQuant only. Merged `MlxParoLinear` retains FP32 trigonometric coefficients, rotations, and affine matmul intermediates for accuracy, but returns FP32 activations from FP16/BF16 inputs. This patch casts only the final projection output back to the input activation dtype. It does not modify packing, quantization, or other methods.

## Accuracy vs independent Torch oracle

title: Use native MLX MXFP8 for exact FP8 inference
body:
## Scope

FP8 only. Compatible E4M3FN tensor/row inverse scaled checkpoints transfer exact FP8 bytes to native MLX MXFP8 matmul. `FP8MlxQuantLinear` keeps BaseQuantLinear validation; compatible layers auto-select this path on MLX. E5M2, FNUZ, E8M0, block scaled, invalid, and unaligned sources retain the dense fallback, now wrapped so FP16/BF16 activations keep their dtype. Packed weights use about 48% less storage than main's FP16 decoded weight matrix.

**Activation dtype:** FP16 inputs yield FP16 outputs; BF16 inputs yield BF16 outputs. The unscaled dot product and checkpoint scaling run in FP32 to prevent intermediate FP16 overflow, then the final result is rounded once to the input dtype. The previous PR revision briefly returned FP32; this revision restores the model's activation dtype as requested. This also avoids propagated FP32 activations and their memory/speed cost.

## Accuracy vs independent Torch oracle

Apple M5 Ultra, MLX 0.32.2. All nine Qwen3.8-27B projection shapes at 1 and 16 rows, with FP16 and BF16 inputs, E4M3FN weights, FP32 row inverse scales and FP16 bias. The independent Torch oracle decodes FP8, divides by inverse scales, and computes matmul+bias in float64. Internal FP32 arithmetic is checked with `rtol=atol=1e-5`; all 36 cases pass. FP16 outputs pass `rtol=atol=2e-3` against the float64 oracle. For BF16, comparison to raw float64 can exceed 2e-3 solely from mandatory BF16 rounding; outputs are compared to a BF16-rounded Torch oracle and must be within one BF16 step or 2e-3. All 18 BF16 cases pass with **zero** rounding violations. Raw 2e-3 ratios above 1 are shown, not hidden. Main's dense FP8 path on `e114733d` returns FP32 for BF16 inputs because it mixes BF16 activations with FP16 weights. title: Add native MLX GPTAQ correction and quantization kernel
body:
## Summary

Add an opt-in MLX GPTAQ correction builder and fused Metal group update. The update follows GPTAQ's sequential weight correction, including the activation correction matrix and cross-group terms. This PR covers one quantization method only.

## What Changed

- Add `gptaq_correction_mlx` for the GPTAQ cross-covariance projection.
- Add `gptaq_quantize_weight_mlx` for dynamic-group GPTAQ weight quantization with 2–8 bits, symmetric or asymmetric codes, and float16/bfloat16/float32 input.
- Add independent Torch-oracle tests for correction construction, dense group updates, quantization boundaries and input casts, plus every Qwen3.8-27B projection.
- Add a reproducible benchmark for all nine Qwen projection shapes.
- The API is opt-in. Processor integration, activation-order permutation, static groups, and MSE search are outside this method-kernel PR.

## Accuracy and performance versus main

M5 Ultra, MLX 0.32.2, Torch 2.14.0, base main `e114733`. Q4 symmetric, group size 128, BF16 weights promoted to float32, float32 inverse-Hessian factor and GPTAQ correction. The full Qwen shape tests use nonzero one-superdiagonal factors to exercise within-group and cross-group corrections. Correction-matrix arithmetic is separately compared to Torch on dense 32×32 and 128×128 inputs for α = −0.5, 0, 0.25, and 1.5.

The timing comparison covers the update stage only: the independent Torch oracle follows main's dense GPTAQ update arithmetic; the MLX path uses the fused kernel and native matrix products. Inputs and correction matrices are already resident in each backend. Each timing is the median of three synchronized runs after one warmup. Hessian factorization, correction construction, and transfers are outside both timings. Torch uses float32 arithmetic; disputed code decisions are replayed at 80-digit Decimal precision from the stored BF16 values and stored float32 correction constants.

title: Fix checkpoint-faithful QVQ mixed and Rank-8 loading
body:
## Summary
- Select each QVQ projection from its serialized checkpoint payload. Dense `.weight` fallbacks stay `Linear`; compressed `.trellis` projections become `QVQLinear`.
- Register serialized Rank-8 A/B/metadata buffers before Accelerate loads the checkpoint. This fixes their previous silent omission when the module registered those buffers as `None`.
- Audit all selected projection tensors after post-init against their serialized payloads. Missing, nonfinite, zero placeholder, and nonmatching tensors fail the load.

## Validation
- Real Seed-7 checkpoint: 80 compressed projections and 32 dense fallbacks load with no unused-weight warning. All required QVQ, Rank-8, and dense tensors match serialized values; three sampled dense projection outputs have relative RMSE 0.0.
- `tests/test_qvq_checkpoint_payload.py` and `tests/test_qvq_vocab_blocks.py`: 15 passed.

## Calibration impact
The existing head Fisher cache was captured using the old Python loader. It does not represent the served checkpoint and must be rebuilt before further tied head/embedding optimization. This PR does not claim revised GSM8K scores.

title: Add native MLX RTN weight quantization kernel

## Summary

Add an opt-in Metal kernel for weight-only RTN quantization. It computes each row group's extrema, scale, zero point, and dequantized weights in one dispatch. The public `quantize_rtn_weight_mlx` function returns MLX tensors matching the existing Torch RTN output convention. It supports 2–8 bits, symmetric and asymmetric quantization, partial final groups, and `group_size=-1`.

title: Add native MLX bitsandbytes weight quantization kernels
body:
## Summary

Add opt-in native MLX weight quantization for bitsandbytes NF4, FP4, and LLM.int8 formats on Apple Silicon. The 4-bit path supports plain and nested statistics. This PR covers one quantization method; processor wiring and inference kernels are separate work.

## What Changed

- Add Metal packers for bitsandbytes 4-bit storage and int8 row codes, plus MLX block maxima and nested-scale reduction.
- Preserve the bitsandbytes 4-bit codebooks and nested 8-bit lookup table without a Torch dependency in the MLX path. The file header credits the MIT-licensed bitsandbytes format tables.
- Add independent bitsandbytes CPU-oracle tests for float16, bfloat16, float32, zeros, signed zeros, subnormals, odd lengths, threshold neighbors, and every Qwen3.8-27B projection.
- Add a reproducible per-projection benchmark. Both APIs are opt-in; checkpoint processor integration remains separate.

## Accuracy against bitsandbytes CPU oracle

M5 Ultra; MLX 0.32.2; Torch 2.14.0; bitsandbytes 0.50.2. Complete Qwen3.8-27B BF16 weight projections, with the model's BF16-to-FP16 cast for int8. The table uses MLX-generated weights; `4-bit nested` is the number of scale **code** differences for each of NF4 and FP4. `Scale drift` is the maximum absolute difference across nested block maxima and offset. All 4-bit packed weight bytes match exactly. All int8 differences are one code at an independently verified exact half step; non-tie differences are zero and int8 row-stat drift is zero.

| Projection | 4-bit byte mismatches (NF4 / FP4) | Nested code mismatches (each) | int8 code mismatches (exact ties) | Max 4-bit scale drift |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `full_attn.q_proj` (12288×5120) | 0 / 0 | 0 | 7679 | 2.38418579e-07 |
| `full_attn.k_proj` (1024×5120) | 0 / 0 | 0 | 615 | 0 |
| `full_attn.v_proj` (1024×5120) | 0 / 0 | 0 | 615 | 0 |
| `full_attn.o_proj` (5120×6144) | 0 / 0 | 0 | 3624 | 0 |
| `linear_attn.in_proj_qkv` (10240×5120) | 0 / 0 | 0 | 6398 | 0 |
| `linear_attn.out_proj` (5120×6144) | 0 / 0 | 0 | 3624 | 0 |
| `mlp.gate_proj` (17408×5120) | 0 / 0 | 7 | 10789 | 2.38418579e-07 |
| `mlp.up_proj` (17408×5120) | 0 / 0 | 7 | 10789 | 2.38418579e-07 |
| `mlp.down_proj` (5120×17408) | 0 / 0 | 7 | 7596 | 2.38418579e-07 |

Nested totals: 21 code differences for NF4 and 21 for FP4 across the nine projections, seven on each MLP projection. The regression test reconstructs block maxima and the mean in float64 from the source weights; each differing lookup decision is within one float32 ULP of a lookup boundary. The largest measured float drift is 2.38418579e-7, below the 1e-6 quantization limit. Int8 totals 51,729 exact-half-step one-code differences and zero differences away from those ties. No packed NF4/FP4 weight-byte differences occur.

## Performance versus `main`

Inputs are already resident in both backends. Each call finishes evaluation before timing ends; one warmup and median of seven calls, excluding input transfer and first compilation. title: Add native MLX FP8 weight quantization kernel
body:
## Summary

Add an opt-in native MLX/Metal FP8 weight quantizer. It returns the exact FP8 storage bytes and inverse scales used by the existing Torch FP8 quantizer, with tensor, row, and block scaling. The Metal kernel multiplies by the selected scale and encodes E4M3FN, E5M2, E4M3FNUZ, or E5M2FNUZ directly. Integer-bit reduction and explicit subnormal handling preserve Torch behavior even for tiny finite weights and infinite inverse scales.

This PR is scoped to FP8 quantization. The current FP8 processor and inference paths still use Torch. E8M0 is dequantization-only in the existing Torch implementation and is intentionally rejected for new quantization here.

## Accuracy and tests

- 157 targeted tests passed on M5 Ultra; Ruff and `git diff --check` passed.

title: Optimize QQQ MLX inference with fused activation quantization and packed 4-bit weights
body:
## Scope
QQQ only. Whole-row QQQ (`group_size=-1`) now transfers its signed nibbles exactly into MLX native 4-bit affine weights. Group-128 QQQ keeps the existing exact 8-bit representation because its per-group rounding cannot be represented faithfully by affine 4-bit scales. A QQQ Metal kernel computes each token's activation maximum, FP16 scale, and quantized codes in one dispatch. Zero and empty token rows are handled.

## Accuracy
- Independent Torch oracle checks exact activation scales/codes for FP16 and BF16 inputs at widths 128, 5120, and 17408, including zero rows and signed extremes.
- Random packed QQQ checkpoints verify exact transferred codes for both supported group sizes (`-1`, `128`) and inference outputs within `rtol=atol=2e-3`.
- All nine pinned Qwen3.8-27B projection shapes verify the native 4-bit and 8-bit QQQ matmul against separate Torch arithmetic at `rtol=atol=2e-3`. The paired performance fixture observed max absolute output difference 0 with its deterministic pattern.
- Focused QQQ/method-selection run: **44 passed**. Full MLX run: **636 passed, 1 failed**; the failure is the existing `test_mlx_generate` fixture pointing to an unavailable local `/monster/data/model/...` path. Ruff and `git diff --check` pass.

title: Add native MLX FOEM quantization group kernel
body:
## Summary

Add an opt-in MLX/Metal kernel for FOEM's default alpha-zero quantization update. It computes per-group FOEM scales and zero points in MLX, fuses the sequential column and beta correction into one Metal dispatch per group, and applies cross-group Hessian updates with the existing accurate MLX matmul. It returns the pseudo-quantized weight, scales, and zero points in MLX arrays. The existing FOEM processor still uses Torch.

## What Changed

- Add `foem_quantize_weight_mlx(weight, inverse_hessian, bits=4, group_size=128, beta=0.2, sym=True)`.
- Match the existing Torch `Quantizer.find_params` and FOEM `alpha=0` arithmetic for 2–8 bits, symmetric or asymmetric groups, and beta in [0, 1].
- Validate nonempty shapes, supported dtypes, Hessian dimensions, finite values, and a positive Hessian diagonal.
- Add an independent Torch oracle, full packed-code reconstruction checks, one-input-step rounding boundary tests, and nine [Qwen3.8-27B projection](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B/blob/1d4bf0f2ff6012fd82039f2fa52739d0dd7c60c0/config.json) tests.
- Add a reproducible per-projection performance benchmark against the corresponding Torch group-update arithmetic.

This is a standalone native API. Alpha-enhanced FOEM/GPTAQ, MSE parameter search, activation-order permutation, and static groups remain on the existing Torch path; those configurations are outside this API. The native path uses `blocksize=group_size` and accepts group sizes 16, 32, 64, and 128.
